body.x: [Las Vegas, U.S. = Aving News] “The collaboration between large enterprises and startups will accelerate the development of the hyper-connected era in the future!”

During our meeting on the 7th in local time at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S., Yong-Moon Kim, leader of the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED), emphasized the importance of startups and the role they will play in the hyper-connected era that will drive the improvement of the quality of human life.

As part of CES 2023, Eureka Park in Venetian Expo Center attracted startups from around the world, including more than 400 Korean startups showcasing their excellent technology. The startups winning 86 CES 2023 Innovation Awards out of a total of 123 given to Korean companies significantly promoted the status and the potential of the Korean industry as a whole.

In particular, the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, an affiliated organization of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, enabled the participation of 51 businesses in CES 2023 by organizing K-Startup Joint Pavilion along with the Seoul Business Agency and Seoul Digital Foundation. KISED has been dedicated to supporting many startups and potential entrepreneurs. The organization conducted a variety of projects last year with a budget of about KRW 800 billion (about 650 million in USD), covering everything needed for startup establishment.

In addition, KISED was instrumental in helping EVAR, an electric vehicle charging solution business, winning Innovation Awards for three areas following their winning for two areas last year. Furthermore, the agency supported startup Raonark, which was founded by seasoned experts with know-how and experience in door lock field. Raonark won three Innovation Awards, attracting attention from visitors.
Behind these achievements, there has always been President Yong-Moon Kim, who supported the birth and development of startups in Korea.
On the 7th in local time at CES 2023, Aving News was able to meet President Kim who has spared no effort for his work to assist startups.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Today marks the third day of CES 2023. How are you finding it so far?

A. President Kim: I think it is a great opportunity. Unlike traditional exhibitions, the portion for Chinese businesses has been greatly reduced, giving Korean companies an opportunity to receive more of the spotlight. Specially, there are about 400 Korean businesses gathered here in Eureka Park, and I take great pride as a supporter of Korean startups for their growth.

They won a whopping 123 Innovation Awards at the event, proving their excellent skills and competitiveness. Among 106 Innovation Awards won by Korean SMEs, 86 of them belong to startups. This figure represents the significant leap that domestic startups are making at CES.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Could you tell us a bit about the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development?

A. President Kim: As an organization under the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, KISED has dedicated itself to supporting the establishment of startups. With a budget of KRW 800 billion won (about 650 million in USD), we empower prospective entrepreneurs and startups with every step of the way to help them establish their business. We offer comprehensive support, offering places for businesses, helping with the administrative process to reach overseas markets, or providing suitable training.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: The common view seems to be that Korean institutions and systems such as KISED are unrivaled in terms of supporting promising companies. What do you think of those claims?

A. President Kim: In fact, visitors from counterpart overseas authorities are often surprised by our system. We've heard many times that they have never seen any agencies around the world offering such comprehensive and systematic support.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: How do the startups gathered in the K-Startup Joint Pavilion assess their achievement in the exhibition?

A. President Kim: It is rather early to talk about the accumulative achievements from the exhibition at this point. However, I’ve heard that a number of foreign investors and local business officials have already come and discussed contracts and agreements by the second day of the event. I should be able to inform you of some good news soon.

body.cap: Yong-Moon Kim, President of KISED at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S. on the 7th (local time) | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: It seems that the industry trends and information that you can get from this CES will be of great help in supporting Korean startups in the future. Can you share any future plans or actions that are already in place?

A. President Kim: I find that the majority of global IT participants in CES 2023 are putting a great emphasis on “hyper-connectivity.” In the past, devices that support IoT functions were only connected with smartphones, whereas recently, the focus has been shifted to controlling each product more conveniently by connecting various devices in a single ecosystem.

In the future, the scope of hyper-connection will be expanded even wider, making it even possible to connect with autonomous vehicles. That will enable passengers in moving cars to enjoy various entertainment at their fingertips. In line with this, we are working on a project called “Ultra-Gap 1000” to support big tech companies for five years to further improve the quality of human life.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: I know that the project has already achieved practical results, with partnerships being formed between large enterprises and startups.

A. President Kim: Yes. The importance of startups to assume detailed roles is growing. That’s because product and technology development has to cover such a wide range that can’t be handled by large businesses alone. Therefore, we are seeking to build a private cooperation system between large enterprises and startups for mutual growth.

body.cap: Aving News Editor-in-chief Joseph Choe (left) and KISED President Kim are posing at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo Center in Las Vegas, U.S., on the 7th (local time). | Photo by Aving News

body.x: Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Due to the nature of startups that always come and grow by introducing new concepts, it seems that they will soon become a major driver of future technologies and visions. What do you think about this?

A. President Kim: I think that's why there are so many visitors here in Eureka Park, where startups of various nationalities are clustered. In particular, Korean startups are receiving attention, and KISED is committed to continuing this trend and offering as much customized support as we can.
Q. Editor-in-Chief Choe: Is there anything you'd like to say to Korean startups participating in CES 2023?

A. President Kim: We are also proud of the large-scale businesses such as Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics with big booths, but personally I take great pride in Korean startups who have been growing with us and showing their outstanding skills at this CES. Keep up the good work.

Meanwhile, CES, the world's largest IT fair, is an exhibition that provides a comprehensive look of the global consumer electronics industry in just one place. It is held annually in Las Vegas in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). Aving News has annually reported on CES news for the world for 17 consecutive years since 2006, hosting the Best of CES which selects the best innovative products and technologies, and the Best of Made in Korea that chooses the most innovative businesses in South Korea. In addition, the media has delivered breaking news about CES through AVING LIVE.
